chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Is'haq ibn Muhammad al-Nakha'i, from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) when permission was sought for a man from the people of Yemen to see him. So there entered a man who was stout, tall, and large. He greeted him (peace be upon him) with the acknowledgment of wilayah, and he (peace be upon him) responded with acceptance and commanded him to sit. He sat down adjacent to me. I said to myself: 'If only I knew who this person is.'

Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'This one is from the descendants of the Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which my forefathers (peace be upon them) had imprinted their signet rings and it was engraved. He has come with it, intending that I should imprint (my seal) in it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it here!' So he brought out a pebble, and on one side of it was a smooth surface. Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) took it, then brought out his signet ring and imprinted it therein, and it was engraved. It was as though I could see the engraving of his seal ring at that very moment: 'al-Hasan ibn Ali.' Then I said to the Yemeni: 'Had you ever seen him before this?'
He said: 'No, by Allah; and I have for a long time been eager to see him, until just now a youth came to me whom I cannot see (anymore), and he said to me: Arise and enter. So I entered.'

Then the Yemeni stood up and was saying: 'May Allah's mercy and His blessings be upon you, O People of the Household — a progeny, one from another. I testify by Allah that your right is obligatory, just as the obligation of the right of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the Imams after him — may Allah's salawat be upon them all.' Then he departed, and I did not see him after that.

Is'haq said: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari said: I asked him about his name, and he said: 'My name is Mihja' ibn al-Salt ibn Uqba ibn Sim'an ibn Ghanim, son of Umm Ghanim; and she was the Yemenite Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and his descendants had imprinted, up to the time of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الأعرابية: The Bedouin woman — the original owner of the pebble, from whom this man is descended; refers to a woman from Yemen who had this stone blessed by Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.الحصاة: The pebble — a miraculous stone kept as a family heirloom across generations, bearing the seal impressions of the Imams
key_terms.الخاتم / خواتيم: Signet ring(s) — used to imprint official seals; the Imams' seals on the pebble serve as authentication of their Imamate
key_terms.السبط: Descendants (sibt) — referring to the Imams descended from the Prophet through Fatima al-Zahra
key_terms.الولاية: Wilayah — the authority and guardianship of the Imam; greeting 'with wilayah' means acknowledging the Imam's divinely appointed authority
key_terms.ذرية بعضها من بعض: A progeny, one from another (Quran 3:34) — cited to affirm the hereditary nature of the Imamate

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the pebble stamped by the Imams in the time of Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a remarkable encounter at the court of Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS), the eleventh Imam, in which a Yemeni visitor presents a sacred pebble that had been miraculously engraved with the seal rings of all previous Imams. The Imam reads the man's unspoken thought — a demonstration of his supernatural knowledge — then stamps the pebble, adding his own seal to the lineage of Imamate seals. The Yemeni's concluding testimony, citing the Quranic phrase 'a progeny, one from another' (3:34), affirms the continuous, divinely sanctioned authority of the Imams as a hereditary spiritual line.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Is’haq Bin Muhammad Al Nakhaie, from Abu Hashim Dawood Bin Al Qasim Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> and permission was given for a man from the people of Al-Yemen to see him<sup>asws</sup>. So there entered a man of plump and tall figure. He greeted upon him<sup>asws</sup> with ‘بِالْوَلَايَةِ’ the Wilayah, so he<sup>asws</sup> returned upon him with the acceptance and instructed him with being seated. So he sat down adjacent to me. So I said within myself, ‘I wish I was aware of who this one is’.

So Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is from the children of the Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble which my<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> had imprinted therein with their<sup>asws</sup> insignias, so it is engraved, and he has come with it intending that I<sup>asws</sup> should imprint (my<sup>asws</sup> insignia) in it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give it!’ So he brought out a pebble and in one side of it was a smooth place. Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> took it, then brought out his<sup>asws</sup> seal and imprinted in it, and it was engraved, and it was as if I could see the engraving at the moment of the seal of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>. So I said to the Yemeni, ‘Had you seen him (Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>) before this, at all?’

So he said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I have been coveting for a long time upon seeing him<sup>asws</sup>, until it was the time when a youth came to me whom I had not seen, so he said to me, ‘Arise, and come in’. So I entered here’.

Then the Yameni got up and he was saying, ‘May Allahazwj have Mercy upon youasws all, the Peopleasws of the Household, [3:34] Offspring of one from the other. I testify with Allahazwj that yourasws right is an Obligatory like the Obligation of the right of Amir Al-Momineenasws and the Imamsasws from after himasws, may the Salawat of Allahazwj be upon themasws altogether’. Then he left and I did not see him after that.

Is’haq said, ‘Abu Hisham Al-Ja’fary said, ‘And I asked him about his name, so he said, ‘My name is Mijam Bin Al-Salt Bin Uqba Bin Sim’an Bin Ghanim Ibn Umm Ghanim, and she was the Yemenite Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> descendants<sup>asws</sup> had imprinted, up to the time of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (8<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah and Ali ibn Muhammad have narrated from Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Nakha’Isma‘il from abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al- Ja’fari who has said the following.

“Once I was in thepresence of abu Muhammad (a.s.) that permission was requested for a man from Yemen to see the Imam (a.s.). A chubby, tall and heavy man then came in and greeted the Imam with the greeting for Wilaya, the Leader with Divine Authority and received the acceptance response. The Imam (a.s.) asked him to have a sit and he sat just next to me. I then said to myself, “I wish not to have been so close to him.”

Abu Muhammad (a.s.) then said, “This is of the children of the Arab lady for whom my ancestors had been printing their seals on a pebble for her and the print would take place. He has brought it with him and wants me to print my seal on it also. He then asked the man to give it to him. The man took out a pebble and on one side of there was a smooth space. Abu Muhammad (a.s.) then took it, brought his seal out, printed on it and the print took place. Even now it is as if I see the print of his (al-Hassan ibn Ali’s) seal on the pebble it. I then said to the man from Yemen, “Had you ever seen him (abu Muhammad (a.s.) before?”
He said, “No, by Allah, I had always was anxious to see him until at this time a young man came to me whom I had not seen before and said, ‘Stand up and come in and I came in.”

The man from Yemen then left saying, “May Allah’s grace and blessings be with you people of Ahl al-Bayt whose each generation is just the other generation. I testify before Allah that it is obligatory to preserve your rights just as it was the case with Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) and the Imams after him, may Allah grant all of them blessings.” He then left and thereafter I never saw him.

Ibn Ishaq has said that abu Hashim al-Ja’fari has said, “I asked him his name. He said, “My name is Mahja‘ ibn al-Salt ibn ‘Aqaba ibn Sam‘an ibn Ghanim ibn ’Umm Ghanim. She was the Arab lady from Yemen that had the pebble on which Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) had printed his seal and also his descendants up to the time of abu al-Hassan (a.s.).”
